verdict.rationale: Gram documents building MCP servers that authenticate through any external OAuth 2.0 provider (Auth0, Okta, Keycloak, or your own), which implies user-delegated tokens. It also brokers connections through the customer's IdP with permissions scoped per server, tool, and team, and ties each tool call to a named employee. However, the evidence frames this around internal employees and teams, not separate connected accounts for each end user of the customer's product, and it never documents per-user credential storage or isolation. Missing for 10: explicit per-end-user connected-account management, per-user scoped token issuance and isolation, documentation of end-user (rather than employee) credential flows, and independent corroboration.
